headline: Bitcoin is steady in the mid-$60,000s ahead of tonight's weekly close, after a Saturday-night wipeout of borrowed bets, as money keeps leaving crypto funds before a heavy week of Fed news, Nvidia results and Anthropic's IPO.

market.asOf: Read at about 19:57 UTC Sun 15 Nov (02:57 Bangkok Mon) from CoinGecko coin pages. CoinGecko's pages showed conflicting 24h figures, so the 24h changes are rough and SOL's is left out. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: Extreme fear: the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index read 10 out of 100 (Extreme Fear), down from 13 a day earlier.

stories.title: Bitcoin steadies in the mid-$60,000s after a weekend wipeout of borrowed bets; the weekly close is at 07:00 Bangkok
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to its lowest level since July late on Saturday (US time) as traders who had borrowed to bet on higher prices were forced out, then bounced about 5%. It has stayed in the mid-$60,000s since. The weekly price candle closes at 00:00 UTC Monday (07:00 Bangkok), when CME bitcoin futures also reopen.
points: Bitcoin fell about 17% from Wednesday afternoon to a Saturday-night low near $62,000, erasing roughly $250 billion in market value, per Yahoo Finance.
The overnight low was $61,946 on Coinbase, and the week opened at $74,757, per CryptoTicker; on Bitfinex it bottomed at $62,029 and then rose 5.5% to $65,487, per U.Today.
About $1.96B of crypto bets were force-closed (liquidated) in 24 hours, nearly 80% of the bitcoin ones being bets on higher prices, per CoinGlass data cited by crypto.news.
Ether dropped as low as $1,715 at 01:45 UTC and is 63.2% below its $4,946 record, per CryptoTicker.

stories.title: Money keeps leaving crypto ahead of a heavy week: the Fed, Nvidia and Anthropic's IPO
stories.summary: US spot bitcoin ETFs, the way many Americans hold bitcoin in a brokerage account, have had a week and a half of withdrawals, and stablecoin supply is shrinking. Futures traders expect the Fed to raise rates in December, and Anthropic's giant share listing is expected this week. Rate odds are market bets, not Fed decisions.
points: Spot bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.91B in withdrawals across seven straight trading sessions (5-13 November), including $185.4M on Friday, per Farside data cited by crypto.news.
BlackRock's IBIT has had 11 straight sessions of withdrawals totalling about $2.35B, per BigGo Finance.
Investors pulled $398.9M from US ether funds between 9 and 13 November, per CryptoTicker.
Stablecoin supply fell $14.2B over 30 days, the biggest drop since June 2022, per Glassnode data cited by Cointelegraph.
CME FedWatch showed an 88.5% chance of a quarter-point rate hike in December on Saturday, per CryptoTicker.

stories.title: Big corporate bitcoin holders under pressure: Saylor hints at a buy as end-of-November deadlines approach
stories.summary: Strategy chairman Michael Saylor posted "This dip could use a little orange," a style of post that has often come before a purchase, but nothing is confirmed until the company discloses a buy. Two deadlines on 30 November matter: MSCI is removing Strategy from its indexes, and Trump Media's noteholders can ask for $1B back.
points: Strategy holds 850,364 BTC bought for about $64.16B, an average of $75,456 each; its last disclosed buy was 1,036 BTC at $79,012 each, per crypto.news.
Miner MARA sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1B and used $750M to repay loans backed by bitcoin, per crypto.news.
MSCI's removal of Strategy takes effect at the close of 30 November; Strategy says MSCI-linked funds held about 13 million of its shares, per Yahoo Finance.

Trump Media noteholders can require it to buy back its $1.0B of notes for cash on 30 November; the company moved 4,259 BTC to Crypto.com on 5 November, which is a transfer, not a sale, per CryptoTicker.

briefs.title: Coinbase stock at its lowest close since February 2024
briefs.summary: Coinbase (COIN) closed at $127.65 on 13 November, its lowest close since February 2024, after dipping to $125.38 during the day, per CryptoTicker.

briefs.title: US moves to seize more than $1.2B stolen in the Binance hack
briefs.summary: The Justice Department says it got court approval to seize more than $1.2B and attributes the 29 October theft of more than $6B to North Korea.

briefs.title: Kava Lend hacked for about $3.8M
briefs.summary: An attacker drained about 55.2M KAVA through a dormant BUSD market and the KAVA token fell nearly 40%; Kava says it is not an infinite mint, per The Block.

briefs.title: Korean exchange Coinone discloses a customer-data breach
briefs.summary: Hackers breached its outsourced customer-support firm on 12 November; Coinone says there is no evidence of a direct intrusion into its trading or wallet systems, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: Zcash holders vote on a dev-fund treasury from Monday
briefs.summary: Voting runs 16-30 November, with options including moving 50,000 ZEC or dissolving the fund, per CryptoTicker.

briefs.title: Russia opens regulated retail crypto trading
briefs.summary: An approved list of BTC, ETH and USDT takes effect 17 November and exchange trading is cleared from 22 November, with retail buyers capped at 300,000 rubles a year per intermediary, per crypto.news.

briefs.title: A bigger bitcoin options expiry lands on 27 November
briefs.summary: About 88,000 BTC of options expire on Friday 27 November, far more than this Friday's weekly expiry, per BigGo Finance.
